title: A lifted top residue cell with a complete cone of shorter amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_{n,T}=(R/\varpi^n)_T$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_{n,T}$, using constant sheaves and inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $M$ is quotient-tower complete if its canonical quotient maps exhibit it as $R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})$, with the quotient transitions and with the terms restricted to $B_T$-scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact and evaluation at $T$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ be quotient-tower complete and write $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T$. Fix integers $a\leq b$ and finite integers $r_q\geq0$ for $q\in[a,b]$, and choose isomorphisms $\theta_q:k_T^{\oplus r_q}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(M_1)$. Assume $M_1$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ after restriction to every site object, meaning $H^j((M_1|_V)\otimes^L_{k_V}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, every site object $V\to T$ and every degree-zero $k_V$-module sheaf $N$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Put $P=B_T^{\oplus r_b}$. There exist a morphism $f:P[-b]\to M$ and a distinguished triangle
$$P[-b]\xrightarrow{f}M\longrightarrow L\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1]$$
such that $L$ is quotient-tower complete and the reduction $f_1:k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to M_1$ induces the prescribed $\theta_b$. Under any zero-differential residue model inducing the $\theta_q$, the map $f_1$ is the top summand inclusion, and its cone has a model which is the direct sum of $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$ and the contractible identity complex on $k_T^{\oplus r_b}$ in degrees $b-1,b$. In particular
$$L\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T\cong\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q],$$
with constant finite-dimensional cohomology and Tor amplitude $[a,b-1]$ after restriction to every site object when $a<b$. If $a=b$ the residue cone and $L$ are zero and $f$ is an isomorphism. Rank $r_b=0$ is allowed, with $P=0$.

proof.text: Identify the literal free coproduct with the finite product used by the lifted-cell API. On each standard generator the specified quotient is the normalized rank-one coefficient projection. Scalar extension preserves this coproduct, so the ordinary free reduction is an isomorphism. The single free complex is bounded above and flat, hence K-flat. The normalized derived adjunction then proves that the exact comparison fixed in the statement is invertible; the quotient is epic, including for rank zero.

proof.text: The complete residue bounds make H^(b+1)(M) zero. The uniformizer triangle makes the top reduction epic. Exact terminal evaluation makes the integral free module projective. Apply the projective normalized lifting argument of the lifted-top-cell module to obtain f with precisely the prescribed top cohomology map. Complete f to a distinguished triangle. The source is complete, and the same module's cone-closure proof identifies quotient-tower completeness with intrinsic local completeness and makes L complete.

proof.text: Derived scalar extension sends the triangle to the normalized residue triangle. Testing the input Tor bound with the unit gives the required cohomology bounds. The first coefficient quotient is a field. Apply the prescribed residue cone theorem. Identify its piecewise zero-differential complex with the statement's coproduct of singles, respecting every inclusion. Transport its literal cone decomposition and derived lower-interval model. Projectivity makes the cohomology map injective on maps from the top cell, proving the equality for every prescribed model. Exact pro-etale pullback transports the shortened cohomology interval, and the field tensor calculation gives the stated Tor interval.

proof.text: If a=b, the residue cone vanishes. The DVR quotient triangles show inductively that all higher reductions vanish. Common K-flat roofs identify these reductions with the terms of the completion tower. Its product is zero, and the completion triangle forces L=0; the distinguished-triangle zero criterion makes f invertible. At rank zero, coproduct extensionality over the empty index type makes the integral free module zero. All constructions also work on the empty scheme.
